title: Lavender Tallow Balm: Yeah, I Put Beef Fat On My Face
body:
Okay so I bought this thing. A tallow balm. Lavender one. Beef fat in a jar you put on your skin, I know how it sounds. My first thought was literally just “what.” Like, why. I was scrolling Etsy late, couldn’t sleep, you know how it goes. Saw this whipped tallow balm stuff. Grass-fed beef tallow. For your face. It was spring, my skin was doing that weird in-between thing—not dry, not oily, just… unhappy. And I remembered my grandma had some old jar of something weird she swore by. Anyway. I clicked buy. Figured it was a weird experiment.

It arrived in a little box. The jar was smaller than I pictured. Cute label. I opened it right there in my kitchen, under that awful fluorescent light. The texture was… not what I expected. Not greasy-greasy. More like whipped butter, but denser. Cold from the mail. I poked it. Smelled like lavender. Real lavender, not the candle aisle at Target. Like, herbal. Almost a bit… green? I don’t know. It was calming though. Seriously. I stood there smelling it for a minute. My cat looked at me like I was insane.

So I tried it. Skeptical as hell.

## Why Beef Tallow For Skin Isn't Actually Crazy

Here’s the thing. I had to look this up after because I was so confused. Beef tallow skincare sounds medieval. But then you read a bit and it’s like… oh. Okay.

It’s basically fat. Suet, they call it. From grass-fed cows. They whip it up until it’s this creamy balm. And the science-y part, the part that made me go “huh,” is that it’s really similar to the oils our own skin makes. Sebum. Our bodies know what to do with it. It doesn’t just sit on top like some plastic-feeling lotion—it sort of… gets it. It absorbs. My brain went to that hotel in Denver, the one with the amazing soap. This was the opposite of that soap. That soap stripped everything. This was like giving stuff back.

Grandma wisdom. That’s the other part. People have been using animal fats on skin forever. Lard, tallow, all of it. For rough hands, for chapped anything. It’s not new. It’s just… forgotten. We got sold on plastic bottles with fifty ingredients you can’t pronounce. And I’ve bought all of them. The $40 creams, the serums, the stuff in the blue jar. My bathroom cabinet is a graveyard of good intentions. This is just fat. In a jar. From France, apparently. Weird.

Anyway. I put it on my hands first. Like a test run.

## What This Lavender Tallow Balm Actually Does

My hands are a disaster. Always dry. Washing them a million times a day, using hand sanitizer that smells like regret. They crack at the knuckles every spring. It’s a whole thing.

So I scooped a tiny bit. Rubbed it in. It melted. Like, really fast. It was cold then warm and then it was just gone. My skin felt… not slippery. Not shiny. Just sort of quiet. Hydrated? But not wet. I don’t know how to describe it. It felt like my skin but better. Not a film. I could use my phone right after, no greasy smears. That was the first “oh” moment.

Then I got brave. Used it on my face. At night. The lavender smell is… it’s strong but not perfume-strong. It’s like a herb garden at dusk. It doesn’t smell like dessert. It smells like plants. It made my whole bedroom smell calm. I have this weird anxiety thing at 3 AM, brain just racing. The smell helped. Honestly. I slept. Maybe placebo, maybe not. I don’t care.

A few days in, I noticed my elbows. I have lizard elbows. Always have. They were… smooth. I showed my partner. “Feel this.” He was confused. But he felt it. “Weird,” he said. “Good weird.”

The jar from that little Etsy shop, “PureLuxeHeritage” or something like that, it’s almost gone now. I use it every night. On my face, on my hands, on this one dry patch on my shin that nothing else fixes. It’s my thing now. I even used it on a paper cut. Healed faster. I sound like a lunatic.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

So it’s been maybe a month? Maybe six weeks. Time is fake.

I’m not saying it’s magic. But my skin is just… chill. It’s not freaking out. That springtime tightness is gone. The random red patch I get by my eyebrow? Gone. I used to have this expensive night cream that came in a frosted bottle. It smelled like flowers and chemicals. It did nothing. This tallow balm does something. I wake up and my face doesn’t feel like it needs to be scrubbed. It just feels like my face.

Is it perfect? No. I still get a zit if I eat too much pizza. It’s not a miracle. But it’s a solid, simple thing that works. It’s one step. I put it on and go to bed. That’s it.

My mom visited. She has psoriasis. Really bad on her hands. I gave her the jar. “Just try it.” She made the same face I did. “Beef fat?” But she tried it. She texted me two days later. “What was that stuff?” She ordered her own jar. That’s the real test, right? If your mom steals your skincare.

## Would I Buy This Lavender Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did.

I’m on my second jar. I keep the first one in my bag for my hands. The new one by my bed. It’s just part of the routine now. It’s not glamorous. It’s a little jar of fat. But it works better than anything fancy I’ve ever bought.

If you’re curious about tallow skincare benefits, I’d say just try it. Start with your hands. See what you think. The whole natural ingredients thing is real with this—it’s literally one main thing. Maybe some lavender oil. That’s it. No mystery list. For rough hands or if you have eczema or just skin that’s pissed off at modern life… it might help. It helped mine.

Anyway. My skin’s happy. I’m sleeping better. The jar is cute. I’m a convert. However weird that is.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yeah. Because it’s so close to our own skin oils, it absorbs and doesn’t just clog stuff up. My face likes it way more than the “non-comedogenic” stuff that always felt gross.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not for me. And I clog easy. It sinks in. It’s not like putting cooking grease on your face. It’s whipped and purified. It just… disappears into your skin. Doesn’t feel heavy.

**What does the lavender tallow balm smell like?**
Real lavender. Like the plant, not a air freshener. It’s herbal and a little earthy. Strong when you open the jar, but soft once it’s on you. It’s relaxing. Makes my pillow smell nice.

So yeah. If your skin is being difficult, might be worth a shot. I got mine from that Etsy shop. No regrets. Just smoother elbows and better sleep.
